title: Takeoff planning from a METAR, a chart supplement and a NOTAM
why_hard: Three independent things must all be caught. (1) METAR winds are reported from TRUE north while runway headings are magnetic: with 15 deg E variation, 260 true = 245 magnetic, giving 5.5 kt of headwind on runway 18 (treating it as magnetic gives 2.0 kt). (2) The grass correction is 15% of the GROUND ROLL, added to both figures. (3) A NOTAM cuts the take-off run available from 2,700 ft to 2,500 ft. Required runway is 2,655 ft, so the takeoff does NOT meet the rule; a planner who misses the NOTAM approves it.
failure_cost: Wrong go/no-go decisions on short grass strips.
sources: ICAO Annex 3 / WMO-No. 306 Manual on Codes (METAR wind direction in degrees true)
FAA Aeronautical Information Manual, Chapter 7 (METAR winds true; ATIS and tower winds magnetic)
FAA-H-8083-25, Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, Ch. 11 (takeoff charts)
